faq.q: How efficient is a petrol car engine?
faq.a: In everyday driving a petrol car turns roughly 20 to 30 percent of the fuel energy into movement. The best modern engines reach about 40 percent at their ideal speed and load.
asks: How much of the petrol makes the car move?

faq.q: Why is exhaust gas so hot?
faq.a: The burning gas pushes the piston down, but it must be let out at the end of the stroke to make room for fresh air. By then it has cooled only partly, so it carries a lot of heat out of the tailpipe.
asks: Why does the exhaust waste energy?

faq.q: Where does the heat from the radiator go?
faq.a: Coolant carries heat from the engine to the radiator, where moving air takes it away into the surroundings. The car heater borrows some of it to warm the cabin.
asks: Why does a car need a radiator?

faq.q: What is friction loss in an engine?
faq.a: Pistons rubbing in cylinders, spinning bearings, gears and the effort of pumping air in and out all use up some energy, turning it into heat.

faq.q: Why are electric cars more efficient?
faq.a: An electric motor turns about 90 percent of its electrical energy into movement and makes little waste heat. It can also recover energy when slowing down, so an electric car uses far less energy per mile.
asks: Do electric cars waste less energy?

facts: Most of the energy in petrol burned by a car engine ends up as heat rather than movement.
Electric motors are often more than 90 percent efficient.
A car's heater reuses waste heat carried by the engine coolant.
